profuse

/pruh-FYOOS/ - the stress falls on FYOOS · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Profuse means plentiful, abundant.

The nosebleed was brief but profuse, ruining a shirt in the thirty seconds it lasted.

Example

When the mayor finally conceded the scoreboard error, his praise for the visiting team turned profuse — three superlatives a sentence, delivered until an aide gently took the microphone away.

Profuse is abundance in motion — the word wants something pouring out: profuse thanks, profuse sweat, profuse blooms. Where 'plentiful' counts a supply, profuse describes the gushing.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

overflowing: Overflowing describes the container that can no longer hold its contents — the inbox, the cup, the laundry basket spilling past its rim. Profuse describes the outpouring itself, abundant flow with no container in the picture: profuse thanks, profuse sweat, profuse blooms.

gushing: Gushing is flow rushing from a single point — a burst pipe, a cut, a fan's breathless praise — with a note of losing control. Profuse pours in quantity without needing one source or any loss of control: sweat, apologies, and blossoms can all be profuse.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

sparing: measured out carefully, no more than needed

skimpy: noticeably less than the occasion calls for

Where it sits · how overwhelming the quantity becomes

ample → profuse → torrential

ample vs. profuse: Ample stops short of profuse — ample fills the need with room to spare, while profuse comes pouring past any need at all.

torrential vs. profuse: Torrential goes further than profuse — profuse blooms and thanks pour generously; a torrential flow overwhelms whatever tries to hold it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pro-: forth

Root — fuse: poured (Latin fundere, fusus)

Put it together: Pro- ('forth') + fus- (Latin fundere, 'to pour') = poured forth. The same pouring root fills transfusion and refund; profuse simply tips the pitcher — whatever it describes, from blossoms to thanks, is imagined as liquid coming out faster than needed.

Use the root in a new word: refund: The theater issued a full refund when the projector failed ten minutes into the matinee.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / vivid

Profuse loves nouns that flow: thanks, apologies, sweat, blossoms, bleeding. For countable stockpiles say plentiful or abundant; say profuse when the quantity streams out of its source — and note the fixed medical phrase profuse bleeding, where the word is standard, not literary.
